ladot__red-book|S-52.1.71.title: Foundation Details (Sheet 4 of 4)
ladot__red-book|S-52.1.71.summary: Shows a 36 in diameter round concrete footing, 60 in deep with 4 in min. topping, for a signal or street light pole with an 11 1/2 in bolt circle. It lists the rebar, anchor bolts, 1 in street light conduit and 2 in traffic signal conduit. Conduit stubs run toward the nearest pullbox, and the bolt circle must be coordinated with the light pole base plate.

sheets.notes:
Foundation details. Sheet 4 of 4.
Plan: 36 in dia. footing (min. 3000 psi concrete), 11 1/2 in bolt circle, 8 1/8 in sq. base, anchor bolts at 45 degrees.
Section: 36 in from curb. Bonding strap or wire. Bushing. 4 in min. topping. 2 3/4 in. 14 in min. to conduit. 60 in footing depth. 6 in min. 36 in dia. 3 in clearance. 2 in clearance. (8) #10 long reinforced. #4 ties at 9 in OC typ. (provide (2) ties at 2 in OC at top). 1 in dia. street light conduit. 2 in dia. traffic signal conduit. Anchor bolts 1 1/8 in x 40 in x 4 in (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt) (ASTM F1554 Gr 55 bolts).
Notes:
1. Use 1 in galvanized conduit for street lighting and 2 in schedule 80 PVC conduit for traffic signal unless otherwise specified.
2. Conduit stubs from foundation shall be in the direction of the nearest corresponding pullbox unless otherwise specified.
3. Topping shall be considered as a part of the foundation.
4. Coordinate bolt circle with light pole base plate prior to anchor bolt installation.
5. Coordinate conduit size and placement with electrical prior to installation.

ladot__red-book|S-57.0.title: Temporary Signal for Type 1 Standard
ladot__red-book|S-57.0.summary: Shows a temporary traffic signal on a Type 1 standard held down by a 36 in square steel platform with four 5 gallon cans filled with concrete, locked on with steel coil chain. Heads are 12 in to match the permanent heads being replaced. The standard is set level on slopes greater than 1/2 in rise per foot by grading or wood shims.

sheets.notes:
Temporary signal for Type 1 standard. Sheet 1 of 1.
Use 12 in heads corresponding to permanent heads being replaced.
Platform (top view detail, not to scale): 36 in x 36 in. 36 in sq. x 1/4 in thick steel platform, hot dip galvanized per ASTM 123. Type 1 base with 4 1 in dia. x 3-1/2 in bolts and nuts with 2 washers for each bolt. 3/8 in dia. steel coil chain tied to each 5 gal. block and locked around the Type 1 standard. 5 gal. can filled with concrete, four cans are required, spaced as shown.
Platform (bottom view detail, not to scale): 36 in x 36 in. 2 in high x 1/4 in thick perimeter lip resting on ground. 1-3/4 in x 1-3/4 in x 1/4 in steel angle brackets welded to plate. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in dia. 8-1/2 in dia. bolt circle. 1 in x 1 in notches for cable.
Weight block (not to scale): 5 gal. can filled with concrete, min. weight 90 lbs. 1/2 in dia. steel rod embedded 9 in deep. Block 12 in wide x 14 in high, 4 in rod width, 3 in rod projection.
Type 1 standard (not to scale): street name sign, pedestrian signal, 3/8 in dia. steel coil chain tied to each 5 gal. block and locked around the Type 1 standard. 5 gal. can filled with concrete. Base assembly. "LADOT" or contractor name embossed or welded on at least two sides. 2 in lip. 1 in x 1 in notch for cable.
For slopes greater than 1/2 in rise per foot, temporary standard to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.

ladot__red-book|S-63.1.title: Fittings, Typical, Terminal Compartment and Pole Plate Mounting
ladot__red-book|S-63.1.summary: Shows typical fittings for mounting a signal terminal compartment, side mount or post-top mount, on a signal standard, along with the pole plate for side mountings. It lists the bolts, washers, lock ring, slip fitter threads and teeth counts used. Construction, material and finish painting follow the State of California Standard Specifications.

sheets.notes:
Fittings, typical, terminal compartment and pole plate mounting.
Terminal compartment, side mount: 3/4 in-11 N.C. hex. hd. bolt with lock washer and flat washer, hot dip galvanized. Flat washer and curved washer. Cover. Special tee. 72 teeth. Cable guide, omit on cover. Lock ring. Pipe threads. 5/16-16 N.C. x 7/8 in sq. hd. cup pt. set screw, hot dip galvanized (6 req.). 4 in (min. thread).
Terminal compartment, post-top mount: 72 teeth upper plate. Washer curved to fit standard. Detail "A": 1 1/2 in pipe thread. Detail A: flat washer, 5/8 in-11 N.C. hex. hd. bolt, hot dip galvanized, nut, washer, 3/4 in lockwasher and 7/8 in flat washer, signal standard.
Pole plate for side mountings.
Note: Construction, material and finish painting shall conform to "Standard Specifications" (latest edition), Dept. of Transportation, State of California.

ladot__red-book|S-76.6.title: Visor, 12 in Diameter, Beveled
ladot__red-book|S-76.6.summary: Shows the 12 in diameter beveled signal visor, with the left-beveled version drawn and an ear detail. A right-beveled visor is made by beveling the opposite side. Other details are in LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06.

sheets.notes:
Visor, 12 in dia., beveled.
Left beveled visor shown. See ear detail. Bevel opposite side for right beveled visor.
Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.

ladot__red-book|S-76.3.title: Signal Visors: Long Visor, Tunnel (Pigeon) Visor and Full Circle Visor, 8 in and 12 in
ladot__red-book|S-76.3.summary: Three sheets showing LADOT signal visor types for 8 in and 12 in heads. The sheets cover the long visor (8 in x 18 in and 12 in x 27 in full circle), the tunnel or pigeon visor (8 in x 8 in and 12 in x 12 in), and the standard full circle visor (8 in and 12 in). Each refers to the ear detail on S-76.3 and to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06.

sheets.notes:
Long visor, 8 in and 12 in diameter, full circle (S-76.7).
Long visor, 8 in x 18 in full circle. Not to scale. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.
Long visor, 12 in x 27 in full circle. Not to scale. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.
Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.

Pigeon (tunnel) visor, 8 in and 12 in diameter (S-76.8).
Visor, 8 in x 8 in tunnel. Not to scale. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.
Visor, 12 in x 12 in tunnel. Not to scale. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.
Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.

Visor, 8 in and 12 in diameter, full circle (S-76.9).
Visor, 8 in full circle. Not to scale. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.
Visor, 12 in full circle. Not to scale. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.
Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.

ladot__red-book|S-72.0.title: Pushbutton, Installation
ladot__red-book|S-72.0.summary: Shows how a pedestrian pushbutton is installed on steel and concrete signal standards, with tapped holes and a typical arrangement at the curb. Pushbutton mounting height is adjusted to 42 in above the surface pedestrians are expected to use to reach the button, with a typical 3 ft 6 in height shown.

sheets.notes:
Pushbutton, installation. Sheet 1 of 1.
No. 7 drill, 1/4 in-20 N.C. tap, 2 holes. Parallel to crosswalk. Steel standards. Standard inserts for concrete standards, tapped 1/4 in-20 N.C., for which intended. Concrete standards. Curb. Typical arrangement. Pushbutton. 3 ft 6 in typical.
Adjust pushbutton mounting height to 42 in above the surface pedestrians are expected to access pushbutton from.

ladot__red-book|S-72.1.1.title: Pushbutton
ladot__red-book|S-72.1.1.summary: Shows the LADOT pedestrian pushbutton assembly in post-top and side mounting on signal standards, with push button station housing and 2 in diameter pushbuttons. It shows the pedestrian signal instruction messages, such as Walk, Don't Start, Flashing Don't Cross, and Time Remaining. Mounting hardware is four 8-32 x 3/4 in screws, and construction follows LADOT material specifications 92-052-02 and 92-053-02.

sheets.notes:
Pushbutton. Sheet 1 of 1.
Post-top mounting (see S-51.7 for installation): back of casting shaped to fit 2 1/2 in dia. standard. Sign text: Start Crossing, Watch for Vehicles, Flashing: if started finish crossing, Time remaining to finish crossing, Don't Start, Steady: Don't cross, Timer, Push button to cross.
Side mounting (see S-72.0A for installation): back of casting shaped to fit curvature of standard. Same sign text.
Type 5 and 6 standards only, side mounting (see S-72.0A for installation).
Notes:
1. Pedestrian pushbuttons: see Standard Drawings S-73.0 and S-73.1. Bicycle pushbuttons: see Standard Drawings S-72.2.
2. Mounting hardware consists of four (4) 8-32 x 3/4 in long.
Housing: construction, materials and finish painting shall conform to LADOT material specification 92-052-02 or latest version.
Assembly: construction, materials and finish painting shall conform to LADOT material specification 92-053-02 or latest version. Pushbuttons shall be 2 in in diameter.

ladot__red-book|S-73.0.title: Pedestrian Pushbutton Sign, Non-Actuated
ladot__red-book|S-73.0.summary: Shows the pedestrian pushbutton sign used for non-actuated crossings. The sign is .063 aluminum, powder coated with black legend on a white background and orange hand and timer symbols. The sign text covers Start Crossing, Watch for Vehicles, Flashing, Time Remaining, Don't Start and Steady Don't Cross, with a Timer symbol. Four 1/4 in inside diameter mounting holes are shown.

sheets.notes:
Pedestrian pushbutton sign, non-actuated. Sheet 1 of 1.
1/4 in inside diameter, 4 places (typ.).
Sign text: Start Crossing, Watch for Vehicles, Flashing: if started finish crossing, Time remaining to finish crossing, Don't Start, Steady: Don't Cross, Timer.
Dimensions as shown: R = 1/2 in corner radius, 4 in and 5 in.
Notes:
1. Sign shall be .063 aluminum.
2. Powder coated with black legend on white background and orange hand and timer symbols.

ladot__red-book|S-70.0.title: Bicycle Detector; Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop
ladot__red-book|S-70.0.summary: Two LADOT detector sheets. The first (S-70.1D) shows bicycle detector loops. Case I is a pair of 3 ft loops for bicycle only (bike lane) and Case II is a pair of 6 ft loops for bicycle and vehicle, with winding details and saw cut sections. The second (S-70.4A, sheet 3 of 3) shows the preformed 30 in LRT track detector loop and the Type A LRT detector handhole.

sheets.notes:
Bicycle detector. Sheet 1 of 1.
Winding detail (not to scale): loops 1 and 2. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair. To pullbox. Wire pairs 1, 2, 3, 4.
Case I (bicycle only): loop 1 and loop 2 each 3 ft, spaced 3 ft apart. Pullbox 3 ft 0 in max. from the curb face.
Case II (bicycle and vehicle): loop 1 and loop 2 each 6 ft, spaced 8 ft apart. Pullbox 3 ft 0 in max. from the curb face.
Direction of traffic flow shown.
Saw cut sections:
Sect. A-A: 3/8 in wide, 3.5 in deep*.
Sect. B-B: 1/2 in wide, 5 in deep*.
Sect. C-C: 3/8 in wide, 5 in deep*.
Sect. D-D: 1/2 in max. wide, 5 in deep*, 8 wires max. per 1/2 in sawcut.
Sect. E-E: 1/2 in max. wide, 5 in deep*.
* Depth of slot not to exceed depth of pavement.
Notes:
1. Install four (4) complete alternating turns of loop wires, unless otherwise specified.
2. For stub-out and conduit details refer to page 2 of S-70.1A.
3. See LADOT Material Specification No. 92-081-05 or latest revision.
4. Use Case I loops for bike lane installations. Use Case II loops when vehicular loops are intended to detect bicycles.
5. An octagonal shaped loop or other non-round shaped loop may be used instead of the round loop with prior LADOT approval.
6. Same winding pattern to be used in both loops for Case I with 1 pair from each loop leading to the pullbox.
7. Loops installed in bike lanes with parking shall be placed with the near edge of the loop 1 ft to the right of the bike lane delineation line, unless otherwise specified.
8. Loops installed in bike lanes adjacent to the roadside without parking shall be centered in the bike lane, or between the gutter and the bike delineation line, unless otherwise specified.
9. Any LADOT approved non-round shaped loops must conform to all other specifications shown on this standard drawing.

Light Rail Train (LRT) track detector loop. Sheet 3 of 3 (S-70.4A).
LRT preformed loop details (cont'd).
Preformed loop: 30 in diameter. 3/4 in O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Expansion joint. CVCC tee. 3/8 in O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose to Type A handhole. Twisted tail.
Winding details (not to scale): twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair, to Type A handhole. Pairs 1 and 2.
Type 'A' LRT detector handhole:
Throat dia. 9 in. 4 in min. 12 in total depth, 11-3/8 in inside depth, 8 in min. 6 in min. below the box. 10-3/8 in box width, 1 in wall. 3 in min. around the handhole. Cast iron frame and cover (cover 11-1/8 in, frame 14-1/4 in, marked LADOT). Loop sealant. Ballast, PCC or hot AC to match adjacent roadbed material. Precast reinforced concrete box. Cables of shielded loop conductor pairs. Portland cement concrete. Conduit to termination pullbox, 2 in Schedule 80 PVC (30 in deep). Clean, crushed rock sump.
Notes:
1. Splices shall only be made in the handhole.
2. Splices shall be soldered and water proofed.

ladot__red-book|S-70.3.title: Multi-Lead-In Cable Pair Loop
ladot__red-book|S-70.3.summary: Wiring diagram showing how up to eight detector loops are connected to a 4-pair multi-lead-in cable, with the pair colors and the actuation phase each loop serves. Loops are wired in series in groups of two to four per pair, never in parallel. Typical installation is shown, and two or three pair cable may be used when the signal plan shows it.

sheets.notes:
Actuation/Phase Loops
Loops 1 through 8 are shown along the direction of travel next to the curb line, wired to cable pairs 1 through 16.
4 pair cable colors: blue/white, orange/white, green/white, brown/white.
Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.
Notes:
1. Connect two to four loops in series to each pair. Do not use parallel connections.
2. Do not connect any unused cable pairs.
3. Typical installation shown. Two or three pair cable may be used when shown on signal plan.

ladot__red-book|S-70.1.title: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop
ladot__red-book|S-70.1.summary: Details for detector loops placed in light rail track, for existing embedded track (saw cut loops) and new ballasted track (preformed loops). Shows sections, 4 turns of wire, 5 inch deep saw cut, 2 inch PVC Schedule 80 conduit 30 inches deep, and the detector handhole and termination pull box. Saw cut loops are for existing embedded track only, and preformed loops are used for all new construction.

sheets.notes:
LRT detector for existing track (embedded)
4 turns of wire. Install detector wires in saw cut (5" deep). Fill slot with loop sealant to within 1/16" of top (do not overfill). 5" max. 2" PVC Schedule 80 conduit 30" deep to termination pull box. Sections C-C and D-D show embedded track, P.C.C. or asphalt concrete, subbase, subballast bed and detector handhole.
Notes:
1. Saw cut loops (octagonal or circular) to be used for existing embedded track installations only. See LADOT Std. Dwg. S-70.1.A for inductive loop installation details not shown hereon.
LRT detector for new track (ballasted)
4 turns of wire in a preformed loop. Top of slab even with rail. Detail A, section B-B: ballasted or concrete track bed, concrete track tie, detector handhole, termination pull box, 2" PVC Schedule 80 conduit 30" deep.
Notes:
1. Preformed loop to be used for all new construction.
2. See current LADOT material specification for traffic loop.
3. See page 2 and 8 for preformed LRT loop details.

ladot__red-book|S-78.5.1.title: Pull Box, Types PB-2 & PB-3
ladot__red-book|S-78.5.1.summary: Section of the standard traffic signal pull box with a lid marked TRAFFIC SIGNAL in 1 inch letters, set flush with finished grade on crushed rock. Outside dimensions are 15 by 25 inches for Type PB2 and 22 by 34 inches for Type PB3. Conduit bonding requirements are given in the notes.

sheets.notes:
Traffic signal pull box section. 1" letters cast or stamped in lid reading TRAFFIC SIGNAL. Finish grade at top of box (see Note 3). Crushed rock under box, 6" min.
Notes:
1. Pullbox details not shown on this plan shall conform to Dept. of Public Works Standard Drawing # L-201-0.
2. Outside dimension: Type PB2 - 15"x25", Type PB3 - 22"x34".
3. Galvanized conduits must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.

ladot__red-book|S-78.5.2.title: Metal Cover Traffic Pull Box (Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T))
ladot__red-book|S-78.5.2.summary: Metal covered traffic pull box for driveways, alleys and locations with vehicular traffic, based on Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T). Shows a reinforced steel cover with embossed non-skid pattern, a galvanized Z-bar frame, special concrete footing, bonding jumper and hold-down bolts. Notes cover placement relative to grade, curbs and poles, cover marking and bonding.

sheets.notes:
Notes:
1. Traffic pullboxes in driveways, alleys and locations with vehicular traffic shall be metal covered per this standard.
2. Pullbox details not shown on this plan shall conform to Caltrans Standard Plan ES-8.
3. Traffic pullbox shall be provided with steel cover and special concrete footing. Steel cover shall have embossed non-skid pattern.
4. Galvanized conduits must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.
5. Top of pull boxes shall be flush with surrounding grade or top of adjacent curb, except that in unpaved areas where pull box is not immediately adjacent to and protected by a concrete foundation, pole or other protective construction, the box shall be placed with its top 1 1/4" above surrounding grade. Where practicable, pull boxes shown in the vicinity of curbs shall be placed adjacent to the back of curb, and pull boxes shown adjacent to standards shall be placed on side of foundation facing away from traffic, unless otherwise noted. When pull box is installed in sidewalk area, the depth of the pull box shall be adjusted so that the top of the pull box is flush with the sidewalk.
6. Pull box cover shall be marked "TRAFFIC SIGNAL".
7. Bonding jumper for metal covers shall be flat braided strap, 2' long minimum, Panduit Part # BS202446EU or equivalent.
8. Hold-down bolt shall be 5/8" and coarse threaded.
Details: reinforced steel plate cover, galvanized after fabrication, with galvanized Z-bar welded frame, lift hole, hold-down bolt, grounding bushing, PCC footing and 6" min. crushed rock all around.

ladot__red-book|S-78.5.3.title: Composite Pull Box, Types PB-2 & PB-3
ladot__red-book|S-78.5.3.summary: Polymer concrete pull box for non-traffic areas with a non-skid polymer concrete cover marked TRAFFIC SIGNAL. Includes installation section and side view, cover details, captive bolt and threaded insert details, and a nominal dimensions table for Types PB2 and PB3. Boxes may be stacked no more than two deep.

sheets.notes:
Installation details: top flush with finished grade, 1" crushed rock base, conduits enter through mouse hole knockouts, see Note 2.
Cover: polymer concrete cover with non-skid surface, TRAFFIC SIGNAL in 7/8" letters, 4" x 1/2" pull slots with 3/16" center pin, manufacturer's logo, load rating, recess in cover for hardware (x2).
Typical cover captive bolt (or similar): 1/2"-13 coarse thread stainless steel penta head bolt, stainless steel flat washer, cast-in bolt gripper, 1/2"-13 unified national coarse thread jam nut with threadlocker.
Typical threaded insert (or similar): insert with drainage hole.
Box: polymer concrete box, open base, 3" x 4-1/4" mouse hole knockouts both end (2X).
Nominal dimensions table
Pull box type PB2: min. depth box (D) 12", min. depth extension (E) 10", LI min 1'-8", WI min 11". Cover: TE 2", B 1 3/4", L 1'-11 1/4", W 1'-1 3/4".
Pull box type PB3: min. depth box (D) 12", min. depth extension (E) 10", LI min 2'-4 1/4", WI min 1'-3 1/4". Cover: TE 2", B 2", L 2'-6 1/2", W 1'-5 1/2".
Notes:
1. Refer to Dept. of Public Works Standard Drawing # L-201-1 for additional details and requirements.
2. Galvanized conduits in pull box must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.
3. Pull box to be used in non-traffic areas, may be stacked no more than two deep.
4. Stencil TRAFFIC SIGNAL in 1" lettering on backside of cover and inside of box.

ladot__red-book|S-52.2.2.title: CIDH Foundation, Type F-2
ladot__red-book|S-52.2.2.summary: Cast-in-drilled-hole concrete foundation for signal and lighting standards. Shows a 30 inch diameter shaft with a reinforcing cage and four anchor bolts on an 11 1/2 inch bolt circle. Depth is 5 feet where at least 100 sq ft of concrete sidewalk is adjacent to the foundation and 7 feet 3 inches without it.

sheets.notes:
30" dia. shaft, 11 1/2" bolt circle, 8 1/8" sq. base plate area, 2" clearance.
Reinforcing cage: 26" dia. (O.D.). Total 12 #7 vertical bars, #4 @ 6" or #4 spiral @ 6" pitch with 1'-6" lap at splice. Overall height 4'-6" or 6'-9".
Concrete 560-C-3250. Bonding strap or wire.
Anchor bolts 18" x 40" x 4" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt).
Depth: 5' with 100 sq-ft (minimum) concrete sidewalk adjacent to foundation. 7'-3" without 100 sq-ft (minimum) concrete sidewalk adjacent to foundation.
Notes:
1. Use 1" galvanized conduit for street lighting and 2" schedule 80 PVC conduit for traffic signal unless otherwise specified.
2. Conduit stubs from foundation shall be in the direction of the nearest corresponding pullbox unless otherwise specified.

ladot__red-book|S-52.1.3.title: Foundation, Type F-332
ladot__red-book|S-52.1.3.summary: Foundation for a traffic signal controller cabinet, shown in top view and side view. Cabinet is mounted on a 24 by 36 inch concrete slab with four anchor bolts, a 3/4 by 8 foot copper weld ground rod, and 30 inch deep conduit. Pull boxes must not be located within the 24 by 36 inch slab.

sheets.notes:
Top view: curb, cabinet mounted rear side of cabinet, 36" slab in unpaved area, conduit to #3 pullbox.
Side view: 3/4" x 8'-0" copper weld ground rod, bushing, 3/4" x 15" x 2" anchor bolts (4 required), conduit 30".
Note:
1. No pullbox to be located within the front or rear 24" x 36" concrete slab.
2. See Standard Drawing No. S-79.9B for grounding details.

ladot__red-book|S-79.0.title: Over Head Service and Under Ground Service, Dept. of Water & Power, with Service Grounding
ladot__red-book|S-79.0.summary: Details for connecting a traffic signal to a Dept. of Water and Power electrical service, shown for overhead service (S-79.8), underground service (S-79.9) and service grounding with PVC or galvanized conduit (S-79.9B). Shows the service pole, a PB-3 service pullbox 5 to 15 feet from the pole, 2 inch conduits, wire sizes, a 60 amp in-line fuse and the ground rod and bonding. DWP installs the #2 aluminum service wires and the contractor installs a continuous dedicated #6 green ground to the controller cabinet.

sheets.notes:
Overhead service (S-79.8)
Pullbox cover marked: Service T.S. & S.L.
3 #2 Alum. wires by DWP. Neutral. 6 #6 standard copper wires (12" long) by DWP. 60 Amp fuse in-line waterproof fuseholder for traffic signals. #6 traffic signal service wires. #6 spare for traffic signal (when specified). 3 #6 wires for B.S.L. (see street lighting plan). Bond neutral to ground rod.
Service pole with 2" conduit, 10'-0" to the pole detail, pullbox 5'-0" to 15'-0" from the pole. Service pullbox PB-3, 14" min. One traffic signal service conduit (2"). One street lighting service conduit when specified on Bureau of Street Lighting plan. Bonding wire. Install ground rod.
Notes:
1. Department of Water & Power to install 3 #2 stranded aluminum wires from service pole to pullbox. At the terminus of each #2 aluminum wire the Dept. of Water & Power to splice 2 #6 stranded copper wires (12" long) using compression type connectors. The exposed ends of each copper wire shall be taped when not in use.
2. Install continuous and dedicated #6 green service ground conductor to controller cabinet.
3. See Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, Sec. 307-2.8.
4. See Standard Drawing S-79.9B for grounding details.

Underground service (S-79.9)
Pullbox cover for combination service marked: Service T.S. & S.L.
3 #2 Alum. wires by DWP. Neutral. 6 #6 standard copper wires (12" long) by DWP. 60 Amp fuse in-line waterproof fuseholder for traffic signals. #6 traffic signal service wires. #6 spare for traffic signal (when specified). 3 #6 wires for B.S.L. (see street lighting plan). Bond neutral to ground rod.
Service pullbox PB-3. Conduit and wires by DWP from manhole. One traffic signal service conduit (2"). One street lighting service conduit when specified on Bureau of Street Lighting plan. Bonding wire. Install ground rod.
Notes:
1. Department of Water & Power to install 3 #2 stranded aluminum wires from service pole to pullbox. At the terminus of each #2 aluminum wire the Dept. of Water & Power to splice 2 #6 stranded copper wires (12" long) using compression type connectors. The exposed ends of each copper wire shall be taped when not in use.
2. Install continuous and dedicated #6 green service ground conductor to controller cabinet.
3. See Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, Under Ground Service, Sec. 307-2.8.
4. See Standard Drawing S-79.9B for grounding details.

Service grounding (S-79.9B)
PVC conduit system
Note: Use a ground rod wire clamp for each wire (Acorn).
Service pullbox with compression type fitting and ground rod 8 ft x 3/4". Schedule 80 PVC conduit to traffic signal cabinet. Service ground block, service fuse, equipment ground bus in cabinet. Conductors: #6 black AC+, #6 white AC-, #6 green dedicated service ground, #8 green bond wire. Ground rod: 8 ft x 3/4" at cabinet. Utility green from service.
Galvanized conduit system
Note: Use a ground rod wire clamp for each wire (Acorn). Use a bushing on all metal conduit.
Service pullbox with compression type fitting. Bonded galvanized conduit, Schedule 80 conduit. Dedicated service ground, #6 black AC+, #6 white AC-, #6 green, #8 green bond wire, utility green. Ground rod: 8 ft x 3/4" at service pullbox and at cabinet.

ladot__red-book|S-92.2.title: 34-Foot Cantilever Sign Standard and Foundation Details, and Laminated Overhead Sign Mounting System
ladot__red-book|S-92.2.summary: Sheet 2 of the 34 foot cantilever sign standard shows the base plate, anchor bolts, drilled hole foundation and weld details, plus general notes. Total sign area may not exceed 180 sq ft, and length B may not exceed 22 feet at maximum sign area. A second sheet in this unit (S-45.0) shows how laminated overhead sign panels mount to mast arms with I-beams and U-bolts, with a table of maximum sign sizes and U-bolt sizes by mast arm length.

sheets.notes:
Detail D: 3"x5" hand hole with frame and removable cover, 1" radius corners. Post. Weld detail. 1"x1/4" backing ring. 3/8" dia. drain hole. Top of walk, mortar, base plate, bonding wire, concrete foundation 560-C-3250, conduit. ASTM A-307 anchor bolts 2" dia. x 32" long with nuts and washers, 4 req'd. Bar 5"x1"x22" long parallel to axis of sign. Overall height 2'-8".
Detail E: bar 5"x1"x22" long, 2 req'd, 2 1/8" dia. holes, 2 1/2" typ.
Section A-A: base plate PL 2"x23"x23" long, 17" bolt spacing, 3" edge distances, 12-#8x14 1/2" long equally spaced, 3" dia. hole finish smooth, 2 1/8" dia. hole, #4 spiral @ 3 1/4" pitch, 3" clear, 3'-0" cast in drilled hole foundation.
Weld detail: backing ring, tack weld, 3/8" and 1/8" welds.
General notes:
1. Total sign area shall not exceed 180 sq. ft.
2. Length "B" shall not exceed 22' with maximum sign area.

ladot__red-book|p54.title: Special Mast Arm Mountings (Sheet 2 of 2)
ladot__red-book|p54.summary: Gives the notes explaining when to use mounting items A through E, which are Pelco products or equivalent. sheets.notes:
Notes:
1. Item "A" is the basic mounting design for most mast arm signal installations when standard tenon location on the mast arm cannot be utilized. It uses a 6" tenon length with 2-3/8" outside diameter for plumbizer mounting.
2. Item "B" is used for installation of traffic signal heads, except programmed visibility (P.V.) heads, when it is desired to mount them horizontally or to adjust the height vertically by movement of item "E".
3. Item "C" is used for installation of horizontal or vertical programmed visibility (P.V.) heads. It is equipped with 14" arms which allow for replacement of signal lamps located in the rear of the signal head.
4. Item "D" is used for installation of electric signs.
5. Item "E" is a standard clamp kit designed to be used for fastening items "B", "C", and "D" to mast arms or poles in a vertical or horizontal position.
6. The bottom arms in items "B", "C", and "D" are stationary and are held in place with pipe threads and set screws. The upper arms slide along the shaft and are held in place with set screws.
7. The standard 29" band for items "A" and "E" fits a 4" to 8.6" diameter. Band lengths up to 56" can be used for larger diameter installations.
8. Items "A" through "E" are available from Pelco Products Inc. or equivalent.
9. The 1-1/2" x 1-1/2" aluminum lock nut shown with item "D" is commonly used for signal head and pedestrian head installations.
10. The 4-1/2" x 4-1/2" x 1/4" aluminum plate is used for sign box reinforcement at bracket installation location and must be specially fabricated.

ladot__red-book|p68.title: Inductive Loop Installation (Sheet 2)
ladot__red-book|p68.summary: Gives the sequence for installing inductive loops and the stub-out detail from the street to the pullbox. The pavement is opened at least 42" from the curb face and at least 18" from the edge of gutter, with an opening of no more than 12" x 16". A 2" PVC (SC80) or PVC flex (SC40) conduit with a 45 degree elbow runs from the pullbox pit, at least 18" below street grade, and each stub-out carries no more than 8 loops or 16 wires.

sheets.notes:
Section D-D (not to scale)
Curb and gutter. 42" min. Hot patch asphalt concrete. 16" max. 2" PVC or 2" PVC flex. Existing pavement. Loop wires, 16" max. Loop sealant.

Stub-out detail (top view, not to scale)
Existing pavement, sand, sub base, hot patch asphalt concrete, 2" PVC or PVC conduit, 2" PVC flex conduit.

Notes: Perform loop installation in the following order:
1. Open the pavement at least 42" from curb face and at least 18" from edge of gutter using a star drill or a jack hammer (asphalt concrete only). Open no more than a 12" x 16" area. In cases where there is a concrete bus pad adjacent to the gutter, install the stub-out beyond the edge of the bus pad.
2. Install 2" PVC (SC80) or PVC flex (SC40) from the pullbox pit with a 45 degree elbow at the stub-out as shown. Depth of the conduit shall be at least 18" below street grade.
3. Patch street using hot patch asphalt concrete and sand as shown.
4. Install duct seal where wires enter 2" PVC or 2" PVC flex.
5. Fill sawcut slot with Caltrans approved hot-melt rubberized asphalt sealant. No more than 8 loops or 16 wires per stub-out.

ladot__red-book|p70.title: Preformed Loop Installation
ladot__red-book|p70.summary: Shows a preformed detector loop built from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene with a 3/4" O.D., with 4 turns of continuous #16 TFFN wire, and filled with hot rubberized asphalt. Each loop head has a 5" contraction/expansion joint with a 9" long by 3/4" Schedule 80 PVC cover slide, and the 3/8" O.D. lead-in hose runs in 2" PVC conduit from the pullbox to the pavement slab. Lead-in wires are twisted at least 2 times per foot, and any variation needs design engineer approval.

sheets.notes:
Winding details (not to scale)
6' expansion joint. CPVC tee. 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. CVPC cross. Expansion joint. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) to pullbox. 3'-0" max. Twisted tail.

Section A-A (not to scale)
Detector loop conductors. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Pavement. To detector per plan. Schedule 80 PVC 2" conduit (see Note 7) (typical).

Notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene, with an O.D. of 3/4" inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" Schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wires in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose with seamless fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a Schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.
7. The 3/8" O.D. lead-in hose shall be installed in 2" PVC conduit between pullbox and entry to pavement slab. Loop shall be attached to top of reinforcing bars when used in the pavement slab.

ladot__red-book|p106.title: Trailblazer Sign (Specifications)
ladot__red-book|p106.summary: Specification sheet for the LED trailblazer sign. The sign is 60" high x 60" wide x 8" deep, weighs no more than 115 lbs, uses amber LED pixels (8 LEDs per 1" pixel) with 10" upper case text, and runs on 120V AC. It is used with static freeway overhead guide signs and mounts with a unistrut system.

sheets.notes:
Trailblazer Sign, Specifications (Standard Drawing S-58.16)

Detail "A" (not to scale): slotted hex head machine screw; square nut; aluminum channel and closure strip, weight 0.66 lbs/ft (0.98 kg/m), thickness 0.105" (2.6 mm); pipe clamps, O.D. 6-5/8", thickness 11 Ga, design load 100 lbs.

Specifications:
1. Trailblazer signs to be used in conjunction with static freeway overhead guide signs. Use one or two arrows on the trailblazer sign as appropriate.
2. Sign shall utilize Light Emitting Diodes (LED) for message illumination. The individual LEDs shall equal or exceed in quality those manufactured by Hewlett-Packard, high power AlInGaP amber type, catalog #HLMA-DL00.
3. Sign text shall be 10" U.C. with 1" spacing between each letter and a minimum of one letter width spacing between words.
4. The overall sign size shall be 60" in height x 60" in width and 8" in depth.
5. The weight of the sign (enclosure and all components) shall not exceed 115 lbs.
6. The front face panel shall be contained within an extruded aluminum frame having full welded seams and powder coat painted with high gloss black finish meeting the color standards of Fed. Spec. 595b, 17038.
7. The transparent Lexan front face panel shall be hinged at the top allowing front access to the interior of the sign. Support shall be provided to hold the Lexan panel open during maintenance.
8. A honeycomb formed black anodized screen shall be provided between the LED lamp clusters and the front face panel to enhance resistance to "sun phantom" effect.
9. The sign shall use a closed cell neoprene gasket making the sign watertight.
10. Sign enclosure hardware materials shall be stainless steel AISI 303 for corrosion resistance.
11. An opening shall be made on the bottom side of the sign so that all conductors, enclosed in flexible conduit, may exit from the sign into the cantilever arm. The sign shall be vented in the bottom portion on the opposite end from the conductor opening.
12. The LED elements shall be comprised of individual removable modules. Each LED module shall be composed of 1" pixels (clusters) having 8 LEDs per pixel. One module shall be used for each letter of the message.
13. Each pixel shall be removable or replaceable on the module without the use of any tools other than a screwdriver.
14. The sign shall be equipped with a photoelectric cell mounted on the enclosure to measure ambient light intensity and automatically compensate for ambient light conditions.
15. The LED sign shall be mountable using unistrut mounting system.
16. Sign shall be equipped with a terminal block to provide separate power inputs to each of the text and arrow modules.
17. The sign shall be powered with 120V AC.
18. A full set of proposed sign specifications and drawings shall be supplied to the City prior to manufacturing.

Bureau of Engineering's Geotechnical Engineering Group (213-847-0538) shall be contacted for recommendations if weak soils and/or groundwater is encountered during construction of the CIDH piles.

ladot__red-book|p112.title: Backplates
ladot__red-book|p112.summary: Signal head backplate shapes for one-section through five-section vertical heads and multi-section cluster heads, with a 2-inch yellow retroreflective strip around the border. Width dimension A is 5 inches typical and corner radius R is 2 inches typical. Notes cover nominal 1/8 inch ABS construction, flange, finish and Type XI retroreflective sheeting.

sheets.notes:
Drawing shows backplate outlines for signal heads with one, two, three, four and five vertical sections, a three-section head with a larger lower section, and clustered five-section and three-section heads. 2-inch yellow retroreflective strip. Dimensions A and R, typ.

Notes:
1. The width dimension, "A" should be 5" typ. and the corner radius dimension, "R", should be 2" typ. The backplate shall have a nominal thickness of 1/8". All outside and inside edges shall be formed with a 1/2" to 5/8" flange (inside dimension), turned away from the front surface.
2. For all manufactured signal heads, backplates shall be designed so as to show no background light between the backplate and the head. The fabrication shall be vacuum formed as one piece with a black lusterless, haircell finish on the front side. All surfaces shall be flat and straight without blisters, buckling or warping. Flanges shall be straight, uniform and have a consistent flange dimension throughout.
3. The backplate material shall be compounded from virgin ABS containing 60% styrene, 20% rubber and 20% acrylic. It shall contain ultra violet inhibitors and stabilizers for protection against ultra violet degradation. The backplate must meet a falling dart impact test of 16 ft/lb.

ladot__supplemental-street-design-guide|.title: Table 1-1: Street Enhancements Applied to Functional Classifications
ladot__supplemental-street-design-guide|.summary: Table from Section 1.5 of the Supplemental Street Design Guide showing which street enhancement networks apply to each functional classification. The networks are Neighborhood Enhanced (NEN), Bicycle Enhanced (BEN), Transit Enhanced (TEN) and Vehicle Enhanced (VEN). Boulevards I and II have BEN, TEN and VEN, Avenue I has all four, and standard dimensions for each classification are on Standard Plan S-470.

sheets.notes:
1.4 Applications
A corner radius is required at the intersection of all streets, roads, driveways (Case 3), and alleys. The geometric design of the corner radii will vary based on the street classification, proposed street enhancements, the transportation context, and the type of vehicles.
As noted above, smaller corner radii can improve pedestrian safety by shortening crossing distances (reducing exposure), increasing pedestrian visibility, and decreasing vehicle turning speed. Smaller corner radii also provide better geometry for installing directional curb ramps at each corner, resulting in a straight direction of travel for pedestrians. Smaller curb radii are especially beneficial at intersections with pedestrian and bicyclist activity and intersections where crashes result from motorist failure to yield due to higher right turning speeds.
1.5 Identifying Street Type (Functional Class & Enhancement)
The functional classifications and enhancements of intersecting streets influence the type of vehicles operating on the street and the street design features. The City of Los Angeles Mobility Plan 2035 identifies street types and enhancements throughout the City. The Complete Streets Design Guide (LA CSDG) identifies how street enhancements apply to different functional classifications. These are summarized in Table 1-1.
Table 1-1: Street Enhancements Applied to Functional Classifications
Functional classification*: enhancements that apply (NEN = Neighborhood Enhanced Network, BEN = Bicycle Enhanced Network, TEN = Transit Enhanced Network, VEN = Vehicle Enhanced Network)

Boulevard II: BEN, TEN, VEN
Avenue I: NEN, BEN, TEN, VEN
Avenue II: NEN, BEN
Avenue III: NEN

4.5.2 Location Considerations
Bus bulbs may be located at the near side or far side of intersections or midblock locations based upon transit provider needs and LADOT approval. Bus bulbs may be located adjacent to driveways and alleys as long as the bus bulb design accommodates the needs of the turning vehicles swept path into and out of the driveway or alley (see Corner Radius guidance).

Shelters should be located to not obstruct the sight distance for motorists entering or exiting driveways, alleys, or streets near bus bulbs. This may require the use of non-advertising bus shelters or the elimination of a shelter at some locations. ladot__supplemental-street-design-guide|.title: Figure 6-9 Example of Case B Raised Crosswalk with Sidewalk Culvert (Edmond, OK)
ladot__supplemental-street-design-guide|.summary: Guidance page on raised crossing drainage, covering sidewalk culverts and the Case C option that keeps existing gutter flow. The culvert follows BOE Standard Plan S-322 (at least 4 in of depth) or DL-2327 (may need more depth for a concrete lid). Case C uses a transverse ramp limited to 5 percent slope, so it applies only to streets with cross slope up to 3.33 percent and unrestricted on-street parking, and the raised crossing is 2 in to 4 in above existing pavement.

sheets.notes:
The design of the sidewalk culvert should follow BOE Standard Plan S-322, which requires a depth of at least 4" to install the culvert, or BOE Standard Plan DL-2327 which may require additional depth to accommodate a concrete lid. See Maintenance Considerations for more information on maintenance of sidewalk culverts. The street should be designed such that the sidewalk culvert is visible to all street users. Flexible delineator posts and/or pavement marking should be used upstream of the raised crossing to ensure motorists and bicyclists do not inadvertently use this space (see LADOT Standard Plan 483.1).
6.5.4.3 Case C - Existing Gutter Flow
Where Case A is not feasible, and where a Case B is not desirable, the existing gutter flow should be maintained by sloping the raised crossing down to match the edge of the gutter (see Figure 6-11). This is achieved by using a transverse ramp. This design is only feasible where there is unrestricted (by time of day) on-street parking, which ensures that the transverse ramp occurs outside of the travel lane.
The slope of the transverse ramp is limited to 5%. Therefore, this design is only applicable to streets with an existing cross slope not exceeding 3.33%. On streets with a cross slope exceeding 3.33%, the transverse ramp will not be able to achieve a raised crossing within the parking area.
When this design is feasible, a full height raised crossing may not be achievable. The raised crossing should be between 2" and 4" above the existing pavement. The sidewalk should meet the existing gutter elevation by using a curb ramp. The sidewalk should not be depressed with this design, which would lower the existing curb height, resulting in a wider gutter pan to achieve sufficient stormwater flow capacity.

Section B-B: roadway half cross-section from center of roadway. Edge of pavement, curb faces, existing gutter. 3.5 in height, 2 ft taper, tack coat, 3/8 in mix A.C. standard D2 PG 64-10, 5.6% asphalt binder.
Section C-C: speed cushion cross-section for 14 ft to 19 ft, with 2 ft taper and curb face (width varies). Profile length 12 ft with 6 ft to the crest, 6.0 in typical.

Section A-A: center of speed cushions. Center cushion cross-section, 6 ft wide with 7 ft dimensions, white markings.
Section B-B: roadway half cross-section from center of roadway. Edge of pavement, curb faces, existing gutter. 3.5 in height, 2 ft taper, tack coat, 3/8 in mix A.C. standard D2 PG 64-10, 5.6% asphalt binder.
Section C-C: speed cushion cross-section for 19 ft and greater. 1 ft 6 in tapers, 1 ft max, curb face (width varies). Profile length 12 ft with 6 ft to the crest, 6.0 in typical.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-709.title: Crosswalk Installation
pasadena__standard-plans|S-709.summary: Pasadena standard layouts for marked crosswalks, covering the basic crosswalk, the zebra crosswalk and the continental crosswalk. All striping is 12 in white or yellow thermoplastic or similar material. Bar spacing starts from the street center line and avoids the wheel path, and bars are parallel to traffic flow at skewed or offset intersections. Continental bars are 2 ft wide and 14 ft long, and a 12 in white limit line is typically used only in advance of signalized intersections.

sheets.notes:
Crosswalk installation. Sheet 1 of 3.
Plan shows the approach to intersection and the leaving side of intersection, with the double yellow center line (DYCL), curb face and edge of gutter. Dimension callouts of 4 ft and 12 ft are shown for the crosswalk lines.
All striping shall be 12 in white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material.
White 12 in limit line in advance of crosswalks typically installed only in advance of signalized intersections. Other locations only when specified. In thermoplastic or similar material.

"Zebra" crosswalk. Sheet 2 of 3.
Plan shows the double yellow center line (DYCL), approach to intersection, leaving side of intersection, curb face and edge of gutter. Dimensions shown include 3 ft and a 1.5 ft minimum.
Notes
All striping shall be 12 in white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material.
Spacing of crosswalk bars shall start from center line of street, avoiding wheel path.
For intersections not perpendicular or 90 degrees (skewed or offset), all crosswalk "bars" shall be parallel to flow of traffic.
For crosswalk layout, refer to sheet 1 of 3.

Continental crosswalk. Sheet 3 of 3.
Plan shows the double yellow center line (DYCL), approach to intersection, leaving side of intersection, curb face and edge of gutter. Bar spacing dimensions are shown, unless otherwise specified (may be up to 5 ft at the direction of the Engineer).
Notes
1. All continental bars shall be 2 ft wide and full length 14 ft, white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material.
2. Start of first bar shall be centered to the DYCL, avoiding wheel path. Continental crosswalk "bars" shall meet edge of gutter. For skewed or offset intersections, all crosswalk "bars" shall be parallel to flow of traffic, in thermoplastic or similar materials.
3. White 12 in limit line in advance of crosswalks typically installed only in advance of signalized intersections. Other locations only when specified. In thermoplastic or similar material.
For crosswalk layout, refer to sheet 1 of 3.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-710.title: Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail
pasadena__standard-plans|S-710.summary: Pasadena detail for placing raised pavement markers (RPMs) with different stripe types. Twelve details cover two-way no passing zones, painted medians, left and right turn lane stripes, lane lines, dashed centerlines, reversals into a left turn lane, left edge lines, two-way left turn lanes, and lead-in and lead-out patterns. RPMs are placed at least 150 mm (6 in) from any crosswalk or limit line. Marker types shown are Type D two-way yellow reflective and Type G one-way clear reflective, with lead-in spacing of 6.1 m (20 ft) minimum, 7.3 m (24 ft) standard and 9.1 m (30 ft) maximum.

sheets.notes:
Raised pavement marker installation detail. Sheet 1 of 3. Dimensions in metric with U.S. units in parentheses.
Detail 1: Two-way no passing, with painted stripe. Marker spacing 7.3 m (24 ft). Through traffic side shown.
Detail 2: Painted median. Through traffic side. Spacing 7.3 m (24 ft).
Detail 3: White left turn lane stripe, 200 mm (8 in) stripe, 50 mm (2 in) typical. Spacing 7.3 m (24 ft).
Detail 4: White right turn lane stripe, 200 mm (8 in) stripe. Through traffic side. Offsets 2.6 m (8.5 ft), 2.1 m (7 ft), 5.2 m (17 ft), 2.1 m (7 ft), 2.6 m (8.5 ft).
Detail 5: White lane line stripe. Total 14.6 m (48 ft). Offsets 2.6 m (8.5 ft) and 2.1 m (7 ft).
Detail 6: Dashed centerline. Spacing 7.3 m (24 ft), 50 mm (2 in) typical.
Detail 7: Reversal into left turn lane. Dimensions 3.6 m (12 ft) and 7.3 m (24 ft). Note: this striping is to be used only in the reversal.
Detail 8: Left edge line with single yellow stripe. Median side. 50 mm.
Raised pavement markers to be installed at a minimum distance of 150 mm (6 in) from any crosswalk line or limit line.

Raised pavement marker installation detail. Sheet 2 of 3.
Detail 9: Left edge line without painted stripe. Median, through traffic side. Marker spacing 29.2 m (96 ft) in total.
Detail 10: Two-way left turn lane. Widths 5.5 m (18 ft), 3.6 m (12 ft), 11.0 m (36 ft), 3.6 m (12 ft) and 5.5 m (18 ft).
Marker profiles: 100 mm (4 in) wide, 3.0 mm (0.12 in) reflective surface height, 118.4 mm (0.75 in) overall. Reflective surface angles 28 to 32 degrees typical.
Type D: two-way yellow reflective marker.
Type G: one-way clear reflective marker.

Type D 2-way yellow
Type G 1-way clear
Yellow stripe
White stripe

Raised pavement marker installation detail. Sheet 3 of 3.
Detail 11: Lead-in single yellow line. Dimensions 2.6 m (8.5 ft), 5.2 m (17 ft), 7.3 m (24 ft), 2.1 m (7 ft), 21.9 m (72 ft) minimum, 29.3 m (96 ft) maximum. Even spacing (see notes). Stripe 50 mm (2 in).
Notes
1. Always place beginning and end R.P.M.
2. Distance between R.P.M. varies with length of single yellow lead-in. Minimum spacing: 6.1 m (20 ft). Standard spacing: 7.3 m (24 ft). Maximum spacing: 9.1 m (30 ft).
3. R.P.M. shall not be placed on painted stripes.

Detail 12: Lead-in/lead-out solid white lane line. Dimensions 2.1 m (7 ft), 5.2 m (17 ft), 4.6 m (48 ft) minimum as shown on the sheet, 21.9 m (72 ft) maximum, 15.2 m (50 ft), 7.6 m (25 ft).
Notes
1. Always place beginning and end R.P.M.
2. Distance between R.P.M. varies with length of solid white lead-in/lead-out. Minimum spacing: 6.1 m (20 ft). Standard spacing: 7.3 m (24 ft). Maximum spacing: 9.1 m (30 ft).
3. If left turn pocket is included, the length of lead-in solid white lane line shall equal the length of the left turn pocket unless otherwise specified.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-711.title: Two-Way Left Turn Lane, Single Yellow Centerline, Solid White Lane Line
pasadena__standard-plans|S-711.summary: Pasadena layout for a two-way left turn lane marked with a single yellow center line and solid white lane lines. The plan shows lane widths of 3.6 m (12 ft) and 11.0 m (36 ft) segments, a 7.3 m (24 ft) center line dash pattern, and lead-in white lane line lengths of 21.9 m (72 ft) minimum to 29.3 m (96 ft) maximum. If a left turn pocket is included, the lead-in white lane line length equals the pocket length unless otherwise specified. Raised pavement markers, if required, follow S-710 Details 10, 11 and 12.

sheets.notes:
Two-way left turn lane (yellow). Sheet 1 of 1.
Lane widths 3.6 m (12 ft), 11.0 m (36 ft), 3.6 m (12 ft), 11.0 m (36 ft), 3.6 m (12 ft). Yellow line width 76 mm (3 in).
Single yellow center line: 7.3 m (24 ft) pattern, with 2.1 m (7 ft) and 5.2 m (17 ft) dimensions, 21.9 m (72 ft) minimum to 29.3 m (96 ft) maximum.
White lane line: 14.6 m (48 ft) minimum lead-in with 2.1 m (7 ft), 5.2 m (17 ft) and 7.3 m (24 ft) dimensions, 15.2 m (50 ft).
Notes
1. If left turn pocket is included, the length of the lead-in solid white lane line shall equal the length of the left turn pocket unless otherwise specified.
2. If raised pavement markers are required, see Standard Plan S-710, Details 10, 11 and 12.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-712.title: Pavement Markings for Left and Right Turn Lanes
pasadena__standard-plans|S-712.summary: Pasadena standard for turn arrow pavement markings in left and right turn lanes. Arrows are solid white and centered in the lane. An additional arrow is installed if the turn pocket is 18.3 m (60 ft) or longer. Dimensions of 2.4 m (8 ft) are shown at the arrow.

sheets.notes:
Pavement markings for left and right turn lanes. Sheet 1 of 1.
Dimension shown: 2.4 m (8 ft) at each arrow.
Notes
1. Arrow pavement markings to be solid white.
2. Pavement markings to be centered in lane.
* Install additional arrow if pocket is 18.3 m (60 ft) or longer.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-713.title: Limit Line and STOP Pavement Markings
pasadena__standard-plans|S-713.summary: Pasadena standard for locating limit lines and STOP pavement markings. The standard limit line location is 500 mm back from the curb line or property line depending on the sidewalk condition, and is installed only when authorized by the Traffic Engineer. Where the property line or sidewalk location is unknown, the exact location is set by work order. The limit line extends to the street center line unless channelization requires otherwise, with a distance of 1.2 m (4 ft) minimum to 9.1 m (30 ft) maximum shown.

sheets.notes:
Limit line and STOP pavement markings. Sheet 1 of 1.
Standard location for limit line unless otherwise specified: 500 mm back from the curb line, shown with the property line, back of sidewalk and 2.4 m (8 ft) dimensions.
Condition: known property line and/or sidewalk location. Install only when authorized by Traffic Engineer. Limit line location to be within this area (typical).
Condition: unknown property line or sidewalk location. Exact location to be set by work order.
Extend limit line to street center line unless channelization requires otherwise.
Distance from STOP marking: 1.2 m (4 ft) minimum, 9.1 m (30 ft) maximum.
Notes
1. If existing limit line falls outside hatched area, notify Traffic Engineering before repainting.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-714.title: Layout, 3 m (10 ft) Wide Turn Bay Transition
pasadena__standard-plans|S-714.summary: Pasadena layout for striping a 3 m (10 ft) wide turn bay transition. A five-step procedure establishes points A through H, locating the straight lines and forming the two curves. The diagram is dimensioned for a 27 m (90 ft) transition, using 4.5 m (15 ft) and 9 m (30 ft) segments, with values in brackets for an 18 m (60 ft) transition using 3 m (10 ft) and 6 m (20 ft) segments.

sheets.notes:
Layout 3 m [10 ft] wide turn bay transition. Sheet 1 of 1.
Diagram: start of transition to end of transition, with segments of 4.5 m (15 ft), 4.5 m (15 ft), 9 m (30 ft), 4.5 m (15 ft), 4.5 m (15 ft). For the 18 m (60 ft) transition, use the figures in brackets: 3 m (10 ft), 3 m (10 ft), 6 m (20 ft), 3 m (10 ft), 3 m (10 ft).
Procedure to install transition
1. Lay out points A, B, E and F.
2. Use points B and E to determine a straight line and mark C and D.
3. Mark G and H by measuring in 190 mm (7 1/2 in) perpendicular to lines A-B and E-F (for 27 m (90 ft) and 18 m (60 ft) transitions).
4. Form curves A-G-C and D-H-F.
5. Stripe.
For 18 m (60 ft) transition, use figures in parentheses shown on diagram and proceed with steps 1 through 5.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-715.title: New Sign Post Installation
pasadena__standard-plans|S-715.summary: Pasadena detail for installing a new sign post using a driven anchor and anchor sleeve. The anchor is driven about 1.0 m (3 ft) into the ground, an anchor sleeve one size larger and 455 mm (18 in) long is driven over it, and the sign post is inserted and fastened with drive rivets. Clearance from the curb face is 455 mm (18 in) desirable and 305 mm (12 in) minimum, with at least 2.1 m (7 ft) from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign.

sheets.notes:
New sign post installation. Sheet 1 of 1.
Plan: 455 mm (18 in) clearance from curb face desirable, 305 mm (12 in) minimum. 51 mm (2 in) sq. O.D. (12 gage) sign post. Two (2) holes at 90 degrees in anchor sleeve. Four holes in sign post. Two (2) drive rivets at 90 degrees, 0 mm to 15 mm (0 to 1/2 in) above surface (typical).
Anchor sleeve options: 63 mm (2 1/2 in) sq. O.D. (12 gage) and 57 mm (2 1/4 in) sq. O.D. (12 gage).
Notes
1. Drive sign post anchor into ground approximately 1.0 m (3 ft). Leave one hole exposed above ground for rivet connection.
2. Drive in anchor sleeve which is one size larger than post anchor and 455 mm (18 in) long.
3. Insert sign post and fasten in place.
4. 2.1 m (7 ft) minimum clearance to bottom of the lowest sign.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-716.title: Post Extension and Sign Mounting
pasadena__standard-plans|S-716.summary: Pasadena detail for extending an existing U-channel post and for strap mounting signs on an existing street light or other pole. Hardware includes a galvanized steel post extension with 8 mm (5/16 in) square head bolts, a stainless steel strap, and a galvanized steel mounting bracket with a neoprene washer. Clearance from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign must be 2.1 m (7 ft).

sheets.notes:
Post extension and sign mounting. Sheet 1 of 1.
Strap mounting on existing street light or other pole: sign, 5 1/8 in dimension, 3 mm (1/8 in) fiber washer, 2 each per sign. Galvanized steel bracket with 8 mm (5/16 in) tapped hole, stainless steel button head bolt and square nut, neoprene washer. Stainless steel strap, 16 mm x 0.75 mm (5/8 in x 0.03 in).
Post extension: existing galvanized steel U-channel post, U-channel post extension, 8 mm (5/16 in) square head bolt with square nut and washer.
Note: Clearance from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign shall be 2.1 m (7 ft).

pasadena__standard-plans|S-717.title: STOP Sign and Post Replacement
pasadena__standard-plans|S-717.summary: Pasadena detail for replacing a STOP sign and its post. A 760 mm (30 in) high intensity R1-1 STOP sign is mounted on a 3.0 m (10 ft) long galvanized square tube post that slides into a 610 mm (24 in) long galvanized anchor tube driven about 1.0 m (3 ft) into the ground. The sheet gives tube sizes, hole and rivet sizes, and concrete or consolidated backfill requirements, with a concrete sidewalk sloped to drain.

sheets.notes:
STOP sign and post replacement. Sheet 1 of 1.
Section A-A: 11 mm (7/16 in) dia. hole in each tube for 9.5 mm (3/8 in) rivet. 50 mm (2 in) dimension.
Detail: 760 mm (30 in) high intensity R1-1 STOP sign. 11 mm (7/16 in) hole with 9.5 mm (3/8 in) rivet. Galvanized 62.5 mm (2 1/2 in) O.D. square tube (12 gauge), 3.0 m (10 ft) long, ASTM A446. Galvanized 75 mm (3 in) O.D. square anchor tube, 610 mm (24 in) long, wall thickness 5 mm (3/16 in), ASTM A500 Grade B. Drive 1.0 m (3 ft) into ground. Plug end of anchor tube to exclude concrete. Tamped backfill typical. 305 mm (12 in) minimum to 455 mm (18 in) maximum dimension shown on the sheet.
Notes
1. Concrete shall comply with the latest edition of the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction.
2. Concrete may be premixed, sacked concrete or field proportioned cement and aggregate with water added and mixing occurring on the job site. 2% calcium chloride (by weight of cement) may be added to produce a quickset concrete.
3. Consolidated backfill or concrete sidewalk, slope to drain.

pasadena__standard-plans|S-718.title: STOP Sign Post Extension for Street Name Signs Installation
pasadena__standard-plans|S-718.summary: Pasadena detail for adding a street name sign extension to an existing STOP sign post. A 57 mm (2 1/4 in) O.D. galvanized square steel tube extension with 12 gauge wall (3 mm, 0.118 in) is attached with 9.5 mm (3/8 in) drive rivets through 11 mm (7/16 in) holes, 4 places in the post and 3 places in the extension. Salvaged street name signs and brackets are remounted, and new stainless steel strap and buckle (15 mm x 0.75 mm) secures them to the tube extension or street light standard.

sheets.notes:
STOP sign post extension (for street name signs). Sheet 1 of 1.
57 mm (2 1/4 in) O.D. square steel tube extension, wall thickness of 12 gauge [3 mm (0.118 in)], galvanized.
11 mm (7/16 in) diam. holes for 9.5 mm (3/8 in) drive rivets (typical): 4 places in post, 3 places in extension.
Salvaged street name signs and brackets (typical). Existing mounting holes on STOP sign post.
New stainless steel strap and buckle, 15 mm x 0.75 mm (5/8 in x 0.03 in), for tube extension or street light standard.
